reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the local HealthcareService StructureDefinition report, the resource-review context, the deterministic aggregate, relevant R4/R6 StructureDefinition elements, and behavior reports for direct HealthcareService scope. No direct behavior findings included HealthcareService; shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were treated as context only.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 HealthcareService was trial-use/FMM 2, so the compatibility burden is neutral rather than normative. That softens the presumption against structural redesign, but it does not erase the business and access risk in service-directory contact, availability, and language data.

overall.oneLineConclusion: HealthcareService keeps its identity, but realistic R4 directory implementations need targeted transforms for contact, availability, and language validation while still preserving low-cost compatibility where feasible.

reasoning.thesisMd: This is not a resource replacement or full conceptual rewrite. The same HealthcareService resource remains in R6, and many same-path elements are stable. The material R4-to-R6 burden clusters in three areas: direct telecom moved into richer contact records, direct availability fields moved into the reusable Availability datatype, and communication language coding moved from preferred to required binding. Those changes make a targeted migration program likely for real service directories, but they do not make every additional local break irrelevant.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The migration shape is a moderate targeted remodel. `HealthcareService.telecom` becomes nested contact data in `HealthcareService.contact` using `ExtendedContactDetail`; `availableTime`, `notAvailable`, and `availabilityExceptions` are consolidated under `HealthcareService.availability` with the R6 `Availability` datatype and its added schedule rules; and `HealthcareService.communication` now has a required all-languages binding. Optional R6 additions such as `offeredIn`, `referralRequired`, and richer eligibility details mostly affect R6-to-R4 down-conversion rather than R4 instance acceptance.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: A migration program is already needed for implementers that use common contact or schedule fields, so keeping every old field forever is not the highest-leverage posture. However, migration unavoidability is only partial: preserving low-cost compatibility still matters, especially for changes that are not required by the contact or availability remodel. The `comment` string-to-markdown change is the clearest avoidable low-cost case; terminology guidance for `communication` also matters because required binding failures can be operationally disruptive.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: Deprecated aliases for old contact or availability paths could preserve more R4 instances, but they would duplicate contact and schedule facts in the same resource and create conflict-resolution rules for operational data. That makes those breaks more like local migration chores once the R6 redesign is accepted. By contrast, retaining `HealthcareService.comment` as `string` or adding a separate formatted comment field would preserve old generated APIs and display behavior at modest cost. For `communication`, a less-disruptive design or guidance could require a valid BCP-47 language while clarifying treatment of supplemental local codings.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: The direct OperationDefinitions, SearchParameters, and HttpRestBehavior reports had no findings whose affectedResources included HealthcareService. The 11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings remain relevant ecosystem context for implementers, but they are not counted as HealthcareService-specific migration drivers.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: The independent review agrees with the deterministic aggregate's `Partial` migration unavoidability, `moderate-targeted-remodel` shape, and `preserve-where-low-cost-but-expect-resource-migration` posture. The important nuance is qualitative: contact and availability drive the targeted migration but have real duplicate-representation costs if old fields are retained, while the `comment` primitive change remains a standards-review-worthy avoidable break despite the broader migration.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Confidence is high for computable StructureDefinition changes. Remaining uncertainty comes from absent official R4-to-R6 change rationale, no live terminology expansion for language validation, and the fact that the R6 input is ballot4 rather than a final publication.

findingConsiderations.title: Direct `HealthcareService.telecom` was replaced by nested `HealthcareService.contact` using ExtendedContactDetail
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a hard old-valid/new-invalid path break and a generated-model/API change for common service-directory contact data. It strongly supports targeted migration, but retaining both direct `telecom` and richer `contact` would create duplicate contact representations, so this is not the clearest low-cost preservation candidate.

findingConsiderations.title: Availability details moved from three direct HealthcareService elements into the R6 Availability datatype
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the largest practical reshape: old direct availability fields become invalid in R6 and schedule data must be moved into a datatype with renamed child concepts and additional rules. It is safety/business relevant for service discovery and scheduling, but preserving both old and new schedule shapes would create conflict risk.

findingConsiderations.title: `HealthcareService.communication` binding strengthened from preferred languages to required all-languages
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The element path remains stable, but R4 local-only language or interpreter-related codings can fail R6 required-binding validation. This adds terminology cleanup to the migration program and deserves clear mapping/validation guidance, even though the goal of requiring actual human-language tags is credible.

findingConsiderations.title: `HealthcareService.comment` primitive type changed from string to markdown
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is not usually a hard wire-format break, but it can change generated primitive types, sanitization, and rendering of existing plain text. Because it is independent of the main contact/availability remodel and has plausible low-cost alternatives, it remains the clearest avoidable standards-review item.

findingConsiderations.title: Eligibility gained R6-only value and period fields plus a code-required invariant
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The new value, period, and invariant are optional R6 expressiveness and do not invalidate existing R4 eligibility content. They matter for down-conversion policy, but they do not drive R4-to-R6 migration unavoidability.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds `HealthcareService.offeredIn` self-reference with no R4 equivalent
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This optional self-reference can be useful and lossy when converting R6 back to R4, but it does not reject or reinterpret R4 instances. It is a local reverse-conversion consideration rather than an avoidable R4-to-R6 break.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds `HealthcareService.referralRequired` boolean with no native R4 field
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is an optional forward addition. It may require an extension or policy for R6-to-R4 conversion, but it should not be treated as a resource-level R4-to-R6 compatibility problem.

findingConsiderations.title: Resource $meta-add is removed from R6 core
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared Resource operation change may affect generic server migration, but it is not specific to HealthcareService and no direct HealthcareService behavior finding was present.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is base search-parameter context shared across resources. It should be handled in platform migration planning rather than counted as a HealthcareService-specific resource break.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Publish explicit R4-to-R6 mapping guidance or StructureMap coverage for `telecom` to `contact` and direct availability fields to `availability`, including handling of `availabilityExceptions`, `notAvailable.description`, and all-day entries with start/end times.

Revisit whether `HealthcareService.comment` should remain `string`, gain a separate formatted/markdown field, or otherwise avoid changing generated APIs and literal display behavior for existing comments.

Clarify `HealthcareService.communication` required-binding migration expectations, especially how validators should treat CodeableConcepts with valid BCP-47 language codings plus supplemental local codings and how local-only legacy values should map.
Document R6-to-R4 preservation options for optional R6-only data such as `offeredIn`, `referralRequired`, `eligibility.value[x]`, and `eligibility.period`.

caveats: The R6 input is ballot4, so final R6 content may differ.
No official change rationale, rendered diff, or live terminology expansion was available in the local inputs.
Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were considered as context only and not scored for HealthcareService.

The migration-program conclusion assumes typical service-directory use of contact, availability, or communication data; sparse implementations that avoid those fields may have a smaller migration burden.
